plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: A shrub with bright colored bracts that are often mistaken for petals, surrounding tiny yellow true flowers called cyathia. In frost-free climates it grows into a large landscape shrub up to 4 meters tall, and elsewhere it is widely grown as a festive potted plant.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to winter (November to February)
plants.location: Native to southern Mexico and Central America; cultivated worldwide, with outdoor displays in Mexico, Southern California, Florida, Hawaii, and Australia
plants.funFact: Poinsettias need long nights of at least 12 hours of uninterrupted darkness for about 8 to 10 weeks to develop their colored bracts, which is why they bloom around the winter solstice. The Aztecs called it cuetlaxochitl and used the sap to make a reddish dye.

plants.name: Helleborus niger
plants.description: An evergreen perennial with leathery, dark green, divided leaves and nodding, cup-shaped white flowers that often age to pink. It blooms in cold weather, sometimes pushing up through snow, and provides rare nectar for winter pollinators.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early winter to early spring (December to March)
plants.location: Native to the mountain woodlands of the Alps and northern Apennines in central and southern Europe; grown in temperate gardens in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Despite its name, it is not a rose but a member of the buttercup family. Legend says it sprang from the tears of a shepherd girl who had no gift for the infant Christ, and all parts of the plant are toxic.

plants.name: Hippeastrum hybrids
plants.description: A bulbous perennial producing tall, sturdy flower stalks topped with several giant trumpet-shaped blooms up to 25 cm across, followed by strap-like leaves. In the Southern Hemisphere garden plants flower naturally in the early summer, while in the north, forced bulbs flower indoors.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere early summer (December); forced indoors in the Northern Hemisphere in winter
plants.location: Hybrids derived from species native to the tropical Andes and South America; grown in gardens in South Africa, Australia, and Brazil and as indoor plants in Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Amaryllis bulbs can send up a flower stalk that grows several centimeters in a single day, and a large bulb may produce two or even three stalks in one season.

plants.name: Metrosideros excelsa
plants.description: A spreading evergreen coastal tree with thick, gray-green leaves and gnarled, sprawling trunks, often clinging to sea cliffs. In midsummer it is covered in brilliant crimson flower clusters made of fluffy stamens, which attract nectar-feeding birds such as tūī and bellbirds.
plants.bloomingSeason: Southern Hemisphere summer (late November to January)
plants.location: Native to coastal areas of the North Island of New Zealand; widely planted in Auckland and other temperate coastal cities
plants.funFact: Its flowering around Christmas has made it a New Zealand holiday symbol, and the species is culturally significant to Māori. The largest and oldest specimens can live for several hundred years.
